definitions.explanation: The capacity to endure hardship, frustration, or tedium without giving up. Emphasizes the strength or power aspect of patience.

examples.japanese: {忍耐力|にんたいりょく}が{強|つよ}い。
この{仕事|しごと}には{忍耐力|にんたいりょく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{子育|こそだ}てを{通|とお}して、{忍耐力|にんたいりょく}が{身|み}についたと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think I developed perseverance through raising children.

notes:
A compound of {忍耐|にんたい} (patience, endurance) and {力|りょく} (power, ability). Emphasizes patience as a capacity or strength one possesses, rather than the act of enduring itself.

USAGE:
Commonly cited as a valued personal quality in job interviews, school contexts, and self-improvement discussions. The suffix {力|りょく} frames patience as a measurable ability.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {忍耐力|にんたいりょく}がある — to have perseverance
- {忍耐力|にんたいりょく}が{強|つよ}い — to have strong perseverance
- {忍耐力|にんたいりょく}を{養|やしな}う — to cultivate perseverance
- {忍耐力|にんたいりょく}が{足|た}りない — to lack perseverance

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {忍耐|にんたい} — patience, endurance (the quality itself, without the "power" nuance)
- {根気|こんき} — persistence, tenacity (sustained effort over time)
- {我慢|がまん} — endurance, tolerance (bearing discomfort or restraining oneself)
